overview: The file consists of an unrestricted cover sheet from the United States Political Adviser for Japan, apparently dated November 19, 1946, transmitting General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers Circular No. 11 of November 7, 1946, together with its four enclosures. The circular replaces earlier instructions and establishes detailed procedures for international aircraft entering or leaving occupied Japan through the Tokyo area, including prescribed approach routes and checkpoints, escort and clearance rules, arrival and departure formalities at Haneda Airfield, English-language radio communications, emergency procedures, flight-safety restrictions, and detention of improperly cleared aircraft. The enclosures provide standard light signals, maps of routes into the Tokyo area and the Tokyo area itself, and a chart of radio navigational aids.

subfiles.title: Political Adviser cover sheet for Circular No. 11
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: An unrestricted numbered cover sheet files or transmits the attached instructions governing international air traffic in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The sheet identifies the United States Political Adviser for Japan, bears number 708, and carries the State Department decimal-file designation 894.7961/11-1946. The November 19 date is supplied by the file title rather than visible body text. It also bears a December 8, 1946 filing stamp from the clerk of the U.S. District Court at Hartford, Connecticut.

subfiles.title: Circular No. 11: International Air Traffic in Japan
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers; by command of General Douglas MacArthur
subfiles.to: All countries, agencies, and aircrews flying aircraft into Japan
subfiles.about: The circular prescribes mandatory routes, communications, clearance, arrival, departure, and emergency procedures for international aircraft operating through the Tokyo area.
subfiles.summary: Circular No. 11 rescinds previous instructions and channels aircraft toward Haneda Airfield through specified checkpoints, including Sado, Niigata, Koriyama, Koga, Nagaoka, Maebashi, Fukuoka, Osaka, Kanoya, and O-Shima. It regulates escorts, manifests, passenger and crew lists, minimum altitudes, avoidance of airfields, radio call signs and frequencies, and contact with Tokyo Control and Haneda Tower. Emergency provisions include Ground Controlled Approach, landings at any Japanese airfield when genuinely necessary, and air-sea rescue assistance. Aircraft may not carry mounted weapons, and airfield commanders are authorized to detain aircraft and occupants that lack clearance or violate its terms.

subfiles.title: Enclosure 1: Standard Light Signals
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The enclosure defines portable traffic-control light signals for aircraft in flight, aircraft on the ground, vehicles, and personnel.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure describes a portable directive light with white, green, and red settings and gives its normal daytime and nighttime ranges. It defines green and red signals for landing clearance, continued circling, stopping, taxiing, runway clearance, and takeoff. Alternating red and green flashes constitute a general warning of hazardous or unusual conditions but are not themselves prohibitive.

subfiles.title: Enclosure 2: Air Routes into Tokyo Area
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: A map depicts the prescribed air routes by which international aircraft were to enter the Tokyo area.
subfiles.summary: The page is titled “AIR ROUTES INTO TOKYO AREA” and is identified as Enclosure 2. The OCR supplies only an image marker, so the map's internal labels and route details are not transcribed, though the corresponding routes and checkpoints are described in Circular No. 11.

subfiles.title: Enclosure 3: Tokyo Area
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: A regional map supports navigation and air-traffic procedures within the Tokyo area.
subfiles.summary: The page is titled “TOKYO AREA,” includes the visible label “SADO ISLAND,” and is identified as Enclosure 3. Its principal content is an untranscribed map image intended to supplement the circular's geographic directions and designated approach routes.

subfiles.title: Enclosure 4: Radio Navigational Aids
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: A chart presents radio navigational aids used by aircraft operating under the circular.
subfiles.summary: The page is titled “RADIO NAVIGATIONAL AIDS” and is identified as Enclosure 4. It directs users to the Haneda Airfield Operations Office for current changes in radio facilities and other flight data. The detailed chart appears only as an image marker in the OCR and therefore is not textually recoverable here.

interest: The file provides unusually concrete evidence of how the Allied occupation authorities controlled foreign access to Japanese airspace immediately after the Second World War. Its checkpoint coordinates, radio frequencies, call words, escort rules, GCA instructions, weapons prohibition, and detention policy permit close reconstruction of an international flight into occupied Tokyo. The attached maps and signal instructions also show how communications technology, weather, mountainous terrain, security, and administrative control were integrated into a single aviation regime.
